sources.title: Skydance Film Heads Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein Set Studios Plan, Pledge Paramount and Warner Bros. Will ‘Build and Release’ Own Films

items.title: Skydance's New Film Chiefs Say Paramount and Warner Bros. Keep Their Own Slates
items.body: One day after the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger formally closed, the co-chairs Skydance has installed atop its Motion Picture Group, Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, outlined their immediate plans for the film division. According to Variety, they pledged that both Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures will keep building and releasing their own slates of films. It is a promise about output and identity rather than a strategy memo: two storied labels continuing to operate as labels under one corporate parent. Whether that survives contact with a combined budget is the open question the pledge invites.

sources.title: HBO Max, Paramount+, and Discovery+ "will unify into a single service”

items.title: Three Streaming Services, One Service, 'Over Time'
items.body: Paramount Skydance says the direct-to-consumer streaming services it owns — HBO Max, Paramount+, and Discovery+, the last of which launched in 2021 — will unify into a single service over time, Ars Technica reports. That is the entire plan as stated: no date, no sequence, no word on what happens to the individual brands. Corporate language like this answers the what and skips the when, and it leaves genuinely open whether subscribers end up with one app, one bill, or simply one company selling them three things for a while longer.

sources.title: Long-awaited small craft harbour in Arctic Bay, Nunavut, expected to open in 2030

items.title: A $77-Million Harbour for Arctic Bay, First Announced in 2019
items.body: Nunavut MP Lori Idlout announced a $77-million federal investment to build a small craft harbour in Arctic Bay — a project first announced in 2019 and initially expected to be completed by 2025. The CBC reports the new money is part of a $106-million commitment the government made in 2024. The original completion target has passed, and construction funding is now being attached to a project whose timeline has visibly stretched. Infrastructure in the Arctic is expensive and slow; this is the paperwork of both at once.

sources.title: ABC and Trump's FCC battle in federal court over free speech and jurisdiction issues

discussion.body: The strongest part of ABC's case is the calendar: weeks before an election, licence review stops being abstract.
But a lawyer's guillotine metaphor is rhetoric, and chilling effects are notoriously hard to demonstrate in court.
True — which is why the request is for a judge to step in now rather than wait to measure damage after the fact.

items.title: ABC Asks a Judge to Stop an Early Review of Its Broadcast Licenses
items.body: A lawyer for ABC asked a federal judge on Tuesday to prevent the Trump administration from conducting an early review of the network's broadcast licences, likening it to a looming guillotine execution that was already chilling the network's editorial decisions weeks before the midterm elections, according to PBS NewsHour. Two things sit side by side here: a legal request that a judge block the review, and an argument about atmosphere — that the mere prospect of licence scrutiny alters what gets broadcast. The guillotine image is advocacy, not a finding. The timing, an election season, is the part that makes the argument land.

sources.title: It looks like the Atlantic storm season may finally produce a hurricane

discussion.body: "A big deal because it has not happened yet" is a statement about timing, not about danger. A basin with no hurricane is a quiet basin, which isn't the same thing as a bad season.
The record's starting line is about watching as much as weather: it begins when aircraft reconnaissance, and later satellites, could actually see what the basin was or wasn't producing.

items.title: The Atlantic's Modern Record Has Never Gone This Late Without a Hurricane
items.body:
The modern Atlantic hurricane record dates to about the Second World War, when aircraft reconnaissance began and continuous satellite coverage came later. In that span, Ars Technica reports, there has never been a season without a hurricane — and no season has gone this late without one forming.

That absence is the story. A hurricane has not yet developed this season, and one arriving now would be a big deal rather than business as usual.

sources.title: Calgary councillors call for federal support as Ottawa's counter-tariffs create costly risk, warns city

items.title: Two-Thirds of Calgary's Estimated Tariff Risk Comes From Ottawa's Own Counter-Tariffs
items.body:
A new update from Calgary city administration assigns an origin to the city's tariff exposure: nearly two-thirds of the estimated tariff-related risk Calgary faces comes from the federal government's counter-measures, CBC reports. City councillors are now asking Ottawa for more relief.

Canada's counter-tariffs are its answer to tariffs imposed elsewhere, which leaves the city's largest identified exposure a homegrown one — an awkward position for a municipality petitioning the same government that created it. The figure is a share of estimated risk, not a tally of money already lost.

sources.title: French students lead massive protests against education policies

items.title: France's Student-Led Movement Draws More Than a Quarter-Million Protesters
items.body:
More than a quarter-million people poured into the streets across France on Tuesday, PBS NewsHour reports — a dramatic development for a student-led movement that began at a single high school. In some cities, police and protesters clashed, and French officials condemned what they called extreme violence.

The headcount is the striking part. A protest that grows from one school to a countrywide crowd is no longer a local dispute.

sources.title: Zhang Yimou Says ‘The Three-Body Problem’ Script Is Still Being Polished After Several Years: ‘It Is Very Difficult to Adapt’

items.title: Zhang Yimou Is Still Reworking the Script for His Three-Body Problem Film
items.body:
Years into the process, Zhang Yimou says he is still reworking the screenplay for his film adaptation of "The Three-Body Problem." He gave the update at the opening ceremony of the Busan International Film Festival, where he is president of this year's competition jury, in conversation with festival director Jung Hanseok.

A marquee director's adaptation sitting at the script-polishing stage years after it was set in motion is a useful corrective to how big projects are announced — as commitments rather than drafts.

sources.title: NASA Glenn Invites Phase 1 Proposals for Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory

discussion.body: The procurement is being run as a full and open competition, and NASA anticipates awarding the contract on Dec. 16, 2026. Work will happen both on-site at Glenn and off-site at the contractor's facilities.
A facility solicitation is the least glamorous part of a lunar program, but testing power hardware on the ground is what stands between a mission concept and a mission that can keep the lights on.

items.title: NASA Is Seeking Bids for a Power Lab Tied to Artemis and a Moon Base
items.body: NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is seeking Phase 1 proposals for the design and construction of an Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory. NASA describes Glenn's expertise in power as crucial to the Artemis program, the Moon Base, and the exploration of Mars and beyond. Proposals are due no later than Oct. 30, 2026, at 1 p.m. EST.

sources.title: Skydance Co-CEOs Insist Its Massive Debt Is Manageable And Won’t Shortchange Production

discussion.body: Reassurance from the people carrying the debt is a statement of intent, not proof the debt is manageable. Deadline frames the comments as an effort to calm jitters, which is a different thing from a demonstration.

Still, the worry reported here is narrower than default risk: the question is whether production budgets get trimmed to service the debt. The executives' claim is that content sits inside a planned financial envelope rather than being the variable that absorbs the pressure.

items.title: Skydance Tries to Quiet Hollywood Jitters Over a Debt Load Approaching $80 Billion
items.body:
Deadline reports that Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz moved to dial down Hollywood jitters that the company's massive, expensive-to-service debt load, approaching $80 billion, will force them to shortchange production.

The executives' answer, as the trade paper relays it: "We have a business plan." A longer quote describes a complete financial envelope for running the business, with content counted as a spend.

sources.title: October 2026 Satellite Puzzler

items.title: How NASA's October Satellite Puzzler Works
items.body:
The October 2026 puzzler from the NASA Earth Observatory is a satellite image with the location left unstated, and the challenge is to identify where it shows.

Entrants are invited to go past a bare guess and share the clues they see, where they think the place is, and what makes it interesting or unique to them. What the observatory offers for a correct identification is puzzler bragging rights.

sources.title: Alberta separatists see an ally in Quebec premier-designate St-Pierre Plamondon

items.title: Alberta Separatists Say Quebec's PQ Win Could Change Canada's Politics
items.body: Global News reports that separatist leaders feel the Parti Québécois victory could change the political dynamic of Canada, especially since the party's leader has shown a willingness to support Alberta independence.

sources.title: Thousands of Alberta referendum mail-in ballots invalid due to errors: officials

items.title: Some Alberta Mail-In Ballots Are Coming Back With Missing Declarations or I.D. Problems
items.body:
Elections Alberta says some mail-in ballot packages have been returned with the declaration form missing, with errors, or with problems involving I.D. They are the kind of paperwork defects that put a ballot in doubt.

The same message carries the genuinely useful part: there is still time to submit the correct information. Anyone who has already mailed a package has a reason to check what they signed and what they enclosed rather than assume it will sort itself out.

sources.title: Tigray war may spill over to Eritrea — helped by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's rhetoric

items.title: Ethiopia's Abiy Faces an Opposing Alliance and a Conflict That Could Reach Eritrea
items.body:
DW reports that Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is consolidating power while contending with a regional alliance that opposes him, and with a Tigray conflict that could spill over into Eritrea.

The conditional is doing real work. A spillover would move the fighting across a national border, which is a different order of problem from a war contained inside one country, and it is framed as a risk rather than something that has happened.

sources.title: Asos confirms hackers sent 'unauthorised' notification to app users

items.title: Asos Says an Unauthorised Notification Went Out Through Its App
items.body: Asos has confirmed that an "unauthorised customer notification" was sent through its app on Tuesday, after users raised the alarm. It is the company's own word — unauthorised — and it describes a message that arrived through a retailer's own channel, where users have already opted into hearing from the brand.

sources.title: Froyo's made a comeback. But at £12 a tub will it last?

discussion.body: The product didn't change; the audience might have. Some of the people buying tubs this time may never have queued for one the first time around, which makes it less a comeback than a debut.
A comeback is also a confession that nobody has thought of the next thing. Reviving a category is cheaper than inventing one, and the tell is that we're calling it a return at all.

items.title: Froyo Is Back in the UK, Which Says Something About Trend Cycles
items.body:
Frozen yoghurt was a huge craze in the 2000s and 2010s. Now, the BBC reports, it has made its return, with multiple chains popping up across the wider UK.

Trend cycles rarely resurrect a thing so much as the memory of it. A second act for a dessert works best when the market has forgotten enough to be surprised again — which is why a revival arrives as new chains rather than a new recipe.

sources.title: Skydance To Make Paramount & Warner Bros Lots Specialized, Each Housing Film Or TV/Streaming

discussion.body: The odd part is where the guarantee comes from: keeping both lots isn't a strategy call, it's a term of the state AGs' settlement.
It's a floor rather than a ceiling — the requirement runs "at least" five years, so keeping them longer is permitted.

items.title: TV and Streaming Get a Whole Historic Studio Lot to Themselves
items.body:
Television and streaming are set to get an entire historic studio lot all to themselves, which Deadline frames as a major upgrade for those divisions.

The rearrangement comes with a floor under it. The settlement in the state attorneys general' lawsuit requires Skydance, the combined Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery company, to keep both the Paramount and Warner Bros. lots for at least the next five years. The real estate stays in the portfolio either way; what changes is which medium calls which lot home.

sources.title: Vietnamese police arrest 12 suspected of prowling city streets at night, snatching cats for meat

items.title: Vietnamese Police Arrest 12 in a Nightly Cat-Snatching Operation
items.body:
Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people suspected of prowling city streets at night and taking cats, according to NPR.

State media cited investigators who said the network recruited riders to move through neighborhoods on motorcycles after dark, trapping up to 10 cats a night. The number is what lingers: not a stray animal crossing the wrong path, but a nightly yield.

sources.title: BoC–BoE Sovereign Default Database: What’s new in 2026?

items.title: Two Central Banks Keep the Ledger of Sovereign Defaults
items.body:
The Bank of Canada and the Bank of England jointly publish a database of sovereign debt defaults, updated annually, that provides estimates of the stocks of government obligations in default.

The units are worth noticing. The database measures a stock — obligations that are outstanding and unmet — rather than a moment in time. A default, in this accounting, isn't an event that ends when the headlines do; it's a quantity that keeps sitting on the books.

sources.title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members

items.title: The EU's Enlargement Ideas Are Aimed at Governments Already Inside
items.body:
The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will do two jobs at once: ease the EU's expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries are candidates, not least war-torn Ukraine.

The two-sided framing is the point. A larger union has to be made attractive to the governments already inside it, not only to the applicants waiting at the door.
